meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Мы вдвоём = the two of us. Core Russian adv meaning 'the two of us, together (two)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The two of us live together.
Let's celebrate just the two of us.

examples.text: Ты же обещал: Новый год только вдвоём.
examples.trans: But you promised: New Year just the two of us.

related.gloss: intensified / related adverb (the two of us)

meanings.note: Adds a reason or an obvious truth. Core Russian part meaning 'after all, you know' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: In good spirits, lively. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cheerful, merry, fun').

examples.trans: It is a cheerful comedy about love.

examples.text: Вдвоём нам точно будет веселее жить!
examples.trans: Together we will definitely have more fun living!

examples.text: Да, идём скорее смотреть весёлый фильм!
examples.trans: Yes, let's go quickly to watch a fun movie!

meanings.note: instrumental of вечер used as an adverb

examples.trans: I'm at home in the evening.

meanings.note: Plural 'вещи'. Common feminine noun meaning 'thing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').
Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?

Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to happen', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: Next door, or in the same flat. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'осед'). Common masculine noun meaning 'neighbour' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Hi, neighbours! Listen, buddy, lend me your phone for a minute.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to save, to rescue', paired with 'спасать'.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!

meanings.note: 'ничего страшного'. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трашный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('terrible, scary').
